UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA ALEXANDRIA DIVISION

MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,

Plaintiff,  v.  KATIE HALL, individually; NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED CHILDREN; META PLATFORMS, INC.; and JOHN/JANE DOES 1–6,

Defendants. ____________________________________/

Case No. 1:26-cv-02331

[PROPOSED] ORDER A

(Granting Reconsideration of ECF No. 108 Insofar as It Denied ECF No. 105 and Directing Completion of the Rule 26(f) Conference and Submission of a Discovery Plan)

This matter is before the Court on Plaintiff’s Rule 54(b) Motion to Reconsider ECF No. 108 as to ECF No. 105 (the “Motion”). Upon consideration of the Motion, the memorandum in support, any response and reply, and the record, it is hereby

ORDERED as follows:

1.	Disposition. The Motion is GRANTED. The Order entered October 30, 2026 (ECF No. 108) is MODIFIED insofar as it denied Plaintiff’s Motion for an Order Directing Completion of the Rule 26(f) Conference and Submission of a Discovery Plan (ECF No. 105). ECF No. 105 is GRANTED on the terms stated in this Order. The disposition of ECF No. 103 in ECF No. 108 is not modified.

2.	Participants. Plaintiff and counsel of record for Defendants National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (“NCMEC”), Katie Hall, and Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta”) shall participate in the conference required by Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(f) as directed in this Order. Defendants John/Jane Does 1–6, who have not been identified or served, are not participants.

3.	Completion of the conference. The participants shall complete the Rule 26(f) conference no later than 14 days after entry of this Order.

4.	Format. The conference shall proceed by substantive written exchange among the participants unless the participants agree on another format or the Court directs one. Nothing in this paragraph precludes the Court from directing attendance in person. Transmission of a proposal, the passage of a response date, silence, or a refusal to participate does not complete the conference.

5.	Content. The participants shall consider each subject identified in Rule 26(f)(2) and each subject Rule 26(f)(3) requires the discovery plan to address, and shall attempt in good faith to agree on a proposed discovery plan. Each participant shall state its position on each subject. A participant may, as to any subject, propose deferral, explain why the subject cannot usefully be resolved before the pending motions to dismiss are decided, state a conditional proposal, or record a disagreement. A participant’s proposal that discovery not proceed until the pending motions to dismiss are decided is a position on the subjects identified in Rule 26(f)(3)(B) and (F) and shall be stated in the report. No participant is required to accept another participant’s proposal.

6.	Report. The participants shall file a written report outlining the proposed discovery plan within 14 days after completing the conference and no later than 18 days after entry of this Order. The report shall state the participants’ agreed proposals and each participant’s separately attributed position on each subject in Rule 26(f)(3), including any proposal to postpone, phase, or limit discovery.

7.	Reporting interval. To the extent paragraph 6 requires the report sooner than 14 days after the conference, the reporting interval under Rule 26(f)(2) and Local Civil Rule 26(A)(1)(b) is shortened to that extent. See Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(f)(4).

8.	Attribution. The report shall record agreements as agreements and disagreements as separately attributed positions. The report shall not portray any participant’s disagreement, silence, or nonparticipation as assent. Counsel for NCMEC and Hall shall identify whether those Defendants adopt a position jointly or separately.

9.	Preparation of the report. Plaintiff shall circulate a proposed report to counsel for each appearing Defendant for review before the report is filed. The responsibility for the report remains joint under Rule 26(f)(2).

10.	Incomplete conference. If the conference has not been completed by the reporting deadline in paragraph 6, the participants shall file a joint status report by that deadline. A participant unable to obtain a joint status report shall file its own status report by that deadline. Each status report shall identify the participation to date, the exchanges that occurred, and the remaining obstacle to completion.

11.	Effect of a status report. A status report does not complete the conference, extend the completion deadline in paragraph 3, or excuse further participation.

12.	Discovery and disclosures. This Order directs completion of the Rule 26(f) conference and submission of the discovery-plan report. It does not independently impose or extend a discovery stay. The timing of substantive discovery, initial disclosures, and responses to requests delivered under Rule 26(d)(2) remains governed by the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and any applicable stipulation or express court order.

13.	Proposed postponement. Any party requesting postponement, phasing, or modification of discovery or disclosure obligations may state that position and its grounds in the Rule 26(f) report for judicial determination.

14.	Existing orders. Nothing in this Order decides whether ECF No. 108 independently imposed a discovery stay or modifies any other applicable order.

15.	Further direction. The Court may determine the timing and sequence of discovery and disclosures after consideration of the report.

16.	Preservation. Existing obligations to preserve discoverable information are not modified by this Order. This Order imposes no additional preservation obligation.

17.	Other matters. Except as this Order expressly provides, ECF No. 108, ECF No. 84, and every other order remain unchanged, and every pending motion, objection, and application remains pending on its own grounds.

Alexandria, Virginia

__________, 2026

______________________________

William E. Fitzpatrick

United States Magistrate Judge
